concept.name: Delivery notice
concept.definition: The written notice given by a futures seller of the intention to make delivery against an open short position on a particular date, delivered through the clearing organization; it is separate and distinct from the warehouse receipt or other instrument used to transfer title.
concept.intuition: The delivery notice is the short's formal 'I will deliver' declaration — the document that starts the physical settlement process and lands on some long's desk.
concept.mechanics: Shorts tender delivery notices through their clearing members during the notice period (from first notice day onward); the clearing organization assigns them to longs, typically the oldest outstanding longs, who must then pay the invoice price and receive the delivery instrument. In some markets a long can retender the notice to another long the same day.
concept.failure_modes: A long assigned a notice must fund the full invoice value promptly; being stopped on a notice when the position was intended as a paper hedge creates financing and logistics burdens, and in some contracts the assigned long can only retender within the same session.
concept.misconceptions: Receiving a delivery notice is not receiving the commodity itself — the notice initiates invoicing, and the warehouse receipt or shipping certificate that transfers title follows through the clearing process.
concept.example: A CBOT wheat short tenders a delivery notice on the second business day of the delivery month; the clearing house assigns it to the oldest long, who pays the invoice price and receives the registered warehouse receipt.

citations.source: CFTC Glossary: A Guide to the Language of the Futures Industry
